item.dc:creator: Anthony Faiola

item.title: Azerbaiyán prohíbe el velo en las aulas sin nombrarlo
item.description: El nuevo código de vestimenta escolar del Gobierno de Azerbaiyán abre el debate en las aulas. La norma prohíbe cualquier prenda "incompatible con los principios laicos de la enseñanza" y, aunque no lo nombra, apunta al velo islámico. ¿Por qué un país con un 96% de población musulmana restringe el hiyab en la escuela? ¿Qué pesa el laicismo heredado de la era soviética y qué teme el poder de Ilham Aliyev? En Los Observadores analizamos la medida y sus consecuencias. Fuente: France 24 - Español.
item.dc:creator: Ershad Alijani

item.title: Five EU states announce plans for immigration ‘return hubs’ in Rwanda
item.description: Germany, Austria, Netherlands, Denmark and Greece likely to face challenges to policy criticised as ‘grave moral failing’ Five EU member states have announced plans to set up an offshore centre in Rwanda for people with no legal right to stay in Europe, in a pilot scheme that is expected to face legal challenges and has been denounced as “a grave moral failing”. The five countries – Germany, Austria, the Netherlands, Denmark and Greece – are the first to seek to use the EU’s newly agreed returns law that allows people who have exhausted all avenues of appeal against their removal from Europe… Fuente: The Guardian - World.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer Rankin in Brussels

item.title: ¿Qué tan grande es la brecha laboral de las personas con discapacidad?
item.description: Inicia la Semana Europea por el Empleo de las Personas con Discapacidad (SEEPH), un evento que busca incluir y fomentar el trabajo para las personas con capacidades físicas limitadas, que, a nivel mundial, son víctimas de una amplia brecha de desigualdad. En el Invitad@ del día hablamos con Mari Mar Gómez, socia fundadora y presidenta de INDAR. Fuente: France 24 - Español.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Retrial date set for Lindsay Clancy over killing of her three children
item.description: Lindsay Clancy is due to face a retrial next March over the killing of her three young children. Fuente: Sky News - World.

item.title: Iran's growing exodus of young talent
item.description: Conflict and uncertainty are driving more and more educated young Iranians to consider leaving the country. Fuente: Deutsche Welle - World.

item.title: Rusia asegura que interceptó más de 1.300 drones ucranianos; cientos de ellos apuntaban a Moscú
item.description: Las autoridades rusas aseguraron que interceptaron más de 1.300 drones ucranianos, cientos de ellos con objetivo a Moscú, durante la madrugada de este 16 de noviembre. Uno de los objetivos del ataque fue el puente que conecta a Rusia con Crimea, que tuvo que detener el tráfico por un momento, pero ya habría sido reestablecido. Los ataques entre ambas partes continúan a pesar de los diálogos mediados por Estados Unidos. Fuente: France 24 - Español.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: US aviation shutdown leaves four major airlines facing a $345 million hit after 18,500 cancellations
item.description: On November 13, 2026, the aviation sector faced a massive disruption as over 18,500 flights were canceled across the United States. This chaos was triggered by the Federal Aviation Administration's ground stop due to a malfunction with aging communications technology. Major airlines, particularly American Airlines and JetBlue, struggled the most. Passengers experienced extended wait times and were eligible for refunds. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: Aman Xess

item.title: Prince William and Princess Catherine play street cricket with locals in Mumbai
item.description: Prince William and Princess Catherine play street cricket with local players in Mumbai, India, during a three-day visit for the Earthshot Prize. Fuente: Euronews.

item.title: Venezuela proyecta recuperar su producción petrolera, pero las inversiones enfrentan riesgos políticos
item.description: La industria petrolera de Venezuela comenzó a recuperarse tras la intervención de Estados Unidos. El crecimiento de la producción durante los próximos años dependerá de nuevas inversiones y de la estabilidad política del país. Fuente: Clarín - Mundo.

item.title: León XIV se despide de Perú con un llamado a la solidaridad y reivindica su vínculo con América Latina
item.description: El papa León XIV cierra este lunes su visita a Perú con un mensaje contra el consumismo y las desigualdades sociales, durante una jornada que incluye un encuentro con adultos mayores en Lima y una misa multitudinaria en la Base Aérea de Las Palmas. Fuente: France 24 - Español.

item.title: Trump says he could meet with North Korean leader Kim Jong-un in China
item.description: Trump is planning to discuss nuclear disarmament when he meets with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Shenzhen, China this week. Fuente: Euronews.

item.title: French film star Depardieu drops appeal against sexual conviction
item.description: French film star Gérard Depardieu on Monday dropped his appeal against a conviction for sexually assaulting two women during the filming of a movie in 2021 and issued "sincere apologies" for his past behaviour on set. "For a long time on film sets, I hid behind provocation and ribald humour," Depardieu, 77, said in the statement, withdrawing his appeal on the day it was set to go to trial. "I believed my remarks and some of my gestures would be without consequences" for those involved, he said. "They were not, particularly coming from a powerful figure such as I once was." Publicado también por: BBC News - World, The Guardian - World. Fuente: France 24 - English.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Prague: Thousands of Czechs rally against government media funding plan
item.description: Tens of thousands of Czechs rallied in Prague on Sunday, November 15, against a government plan to cut a public media fee and move funding to the state budget, a policy critics say would dent the broadcasters' independence and viability. Fuente: France 24 - English.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: "Es Pattinson, Robert Pattinson": el actor británico será el nuevo James Bond
item.description: El protagonista de "Crepúsculo" y "The Batman" releva a Daniel Craig y se convierte en el séptimo actor que da vida al agente 007. Fuente: BBC News Mundo.

item.title: UK media regulator tightens curbs on online child abuse material
item.description: Britain’s media regulator Ofcom announced new online child-safety rules on Monday, requiring platforms to take stronger action against child sexual abuse material and grooming ahead of a planned ban on social media access for under-16s. Countries from Australia ‌and Britain to France, Denmark and Turkey are moving to restrict children’s access to online platforms and impose tougher obligations on technology companies over content moderation and child safety. Ofcom’s new measures in Britain would... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.description: Students have taken to the streets to demand accountability from authorities over toxic air pollution in New Delhi. Fuente: Al Jazeera English.

item.description: Eight men killed in shooting near Pietermaritzburg while six men and three women shot dead near Pretoria. Publicado también por: BBC News - World, Sky News - World. Fuente: Al Jazeera English.

item.title: Melissa Auf Der Maur: 90s rock memoirs and photographs
item.description: Melissa Auf Der Maur grew up in Montreal, the daughter of a feminist activist mother and a journalist-turned-politician father. At just 22, she joined Courtney Love’s band Hole as its bass player, going on to become a role model for young female fans – and not only female fans – of alternative rock. She later joined The Smashing Pumpkins before striking out on her own as a solo artist. She dropped by FRANCE 24 to talk to Marjorie Hache about the epic decade that brought the 20th century to a close. Fuente: France 24 - English.
item.dc:creator: Marjorie HACHE

item.title: Dandora, el vertedero de Nairobi donde se sobrevive entre toneladas de plástico
item.description: Cada día, unas 2.000 toneladas de residuos llegan al vertedero de Dandora, en Nairobi, la capital de Kenia. Allí, cientos de trabajadores buscan materiales reciclables entre montañas de basura, expuestos a condiciones que ponen en riesgo su salud. Pese a su esfuerzo, apenas se recicla el 7% del plástico. Un trabajo esencial con un alto costo humano. Reportaje de Bastien Renouil y Élodie Cousin para France 24. Fuente: France 24 - Español.
item.dc:creator: Bastien Renouil

item.title: Hong Kong man arrested at Singapore’s Changi Airport over alleged shop theft
item.description: A 38-year-old Hong Kong man was arrested on arrival in Singapore in October after he allegedly stole earbuds from a store in Changi Airport before leaving the city state nearly three months earlier. Local police said on Monday that on August 2, police were called to a case of theft at a store in the transit area of Changi Airport Terminal 1 after a staff member found a box of earbuds, valued at S$347.71 (US$269.72), missing from a display shelf. Surveillance footage established that a man had... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.description: The Twilight, Batman and Odyssey star's profile will go even more stellar when he plays James Bond. Fuente: BBC News - World.

item.title: American Roosters Fight in the Philippines Despite U.S. Crackdown
item.description: It’s illegal in the United States to transport game fowl for fighting. But investigators say breeders are sending birds to the Philippines, where cockfighting is legal and lucrative. Fuente: The New York Times - World.

item.title: Hong Kong scholar says Musk’s claim that city ‘will be gone soon’ doesn’t add up
item.description: Tech billionaire Elon Musk has weighed in on Hong Kong’s low birth rate, saying that the city’s population “will be gone soon” unless the trend reverses. Musk, CEO of SpaceX and Tesla, was responding to a social media post by former investment banker John LeFevre in which LeFevre said that he had developed “Grok Bot Syndrome” after his AI employees proved fast, efficient and reliable, and he expected the same from real people. LeFevre added that he had become impatient, short-tempered and... Fuente: South China Morning Post.

item.description: Delegates met in Geneva to discuss guardrails for such systems even as their development grows. Russia and the United States have resisted the efforts. Fuente: The New York Times - World.

item.title: Saudi Arabia dismisses commander of anti-Houthi coalition as rebels advance
item.description: Saudi Arabia has removed the commander of the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen, state media said Monday, as the Iran-backed rebels advanced on the temporary capital of Aden. The shake up comes after Houthi forces took territory on Yemen's southern coast and Saudi-backed forces fell back to defend the capital. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: Guinea's gold rush: Arrests, deportations spark outcry
item.description: Guinea has banned illegal gold mining, citing environmental concerns. It has further charged hundreds of suspected local and foreign illegal miners amid reports of rights abuses and deportations. Fuente: Deutsche Welle - World.

item.title: 'Historical fiction is about filling in the gaps', author Ian McGuire says
item.description: A Man Booker Prize nominee has been speaking to FRANCE 24 about his latest novel and his passion for researching and writing historical fiction. Ian McGuire was shortlisted for the prize in 2016 for his novel “The North Water”. His latest book, “White River Crossing”, was published earlier this year and has now been translated into French, under the shortened title “White River”. Fuente: France 24 - English.
